chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said concerning a man who swore an oath out of taqiyyah: he said,

If you fear for your blood or your property, then swear an oath to ward it off from yourself by your oath. But if you see that your oath will not ward anything off from you, then do not swear to them.

key_terms.دَمِكَ: your blood, meaning your life or bodily safety

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to swear an oath out of taqiyyah in order to protect one’s life or property?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on swearing an oath under taqiyyah when a person fears harm to life or property. It permits the oath as a means of protection, but only when it actually serves to avert harm; if it brings no protection, it should not be taken.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4289 - Imam (as) was asked about a man who swore an oath out of taqiyyah (dissimulation).
Imam (as) said: "If you fear for your life or property, then swear an oath to protect yourself with it. However, if you see that your oath will not protect you in any way, then do not swear to them."
